description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to contribute to reducing the regional economic disparities around the Kasserine – Sidi Bouzid – Sfax corridor by improving the quality of road transport access and facilitating access to finance for small and medium sized enterprises.

The Project targets both a key transport corridor and the economic activities around it. This is achieved through two complementary components: (i) Component 1 seeks to improve specific sections of the Sfax – Sidi Bouzid – Kasserine corridor and improve road safety and climate resilience on these sections; and (ii) Component 2 will support complementary interventions to foster economic development through improved connectivity and access to finance to SMEs along the corridor. The project targets western sections of a corridor that ultimately connects inland economic activities with maritime transport at the port of Sfax and Tunisia's coastal motorway network. Component 1: Corridor Infrastructure Development (US$ 166.4 million): The Project will finance road works for three western sections of the Sfax - Sidi-Bouzid - Kasserine economic development corridor totaling 64.7 km (see map in Annex 3). Civil works will include widening and upgrading of the road sections where needed, upgrading of bridges and culverts, improvements to road intersections, traffic signs and installation of other road safety measures. Since the Project location is prone to potential climate hazards, the designs have incorporated measures to increase adaptation to the climatic risks in the region (esp. associated with extreme precipitation events). Road safety audits and results from the Project's ESIA have informed the designs that will be used as the basis for procuring works. For the avoidance of doubt, Component 1 concerns three lots (numbers 6, 7, and 8) along western sections of the economic corridor between Kasserine and Sfax. Component 2: Corridor Economic Development (US$ 48 million). This component aims to maximize the benefits of improved infrastructure by enhancing inclusion and increasing access to finance. It supports works on rural feeder roads in additional investments under CDC which will take place along all sections of the economic corridor between Kasserine and Sfax. Specific subcomponents include:2.1. Land connectivity infrastructure (US$ 33 million). To improve accessibility to the Corridor's rural areas, the project will complement the RN13 improvement by financing civil works to upgrade priority rural feeder roads (115.4 km). This activity will facilitate access to markets through increased connectivity and the upgrade of existing unpaved rural access roads, to all-season and climate resilient roads and road maintenance by local microenterprises. Local small and micro enterprises will be strongly involved in the construction and future maintenance of roads, through labor intensive methods. Priority feeder roads have been selected by the MEHAT in consultation with local authorities based on their connection to main rural areas along the corridor. 2.2. Access to finance (CDC Impact Fund -- US$ 15 million). The Project would contribute to the capitalization of the CDC Impact Fund, a private equity vehicle targeting SMEs in lagging regions, with a dedicated compartment to investments in SMEs in the three governorates of the corridor area, Kasserine, Sidi Bouzid and Sfax. The CDC Impact Fund will provide SMEs with equity and quasi-equity investments through participation in their capital. The CDC Impact Fund will be managed by CDC Gestion, a management company partially owned by CDC and managing other CDC funded vehicles. At least 25 percent of funds will be earmarked for women-led SMEs and will be complemented by (i) tailored advice and training to women to improve their skills in a range of areas such as, legal and financial literacy, and to increase their know-how and networking opportunities, and (ii) advice to the CDC Impact Fund on how to reach out to women entrepreneurs through improved marketing and product development. The project will undertake a rural women's needs assessment for financial and non-financial services to structure the proposed interventions in the most targeted and effective way for the rural communities. Lastly, climate resilience training will be devised to beneficiary SMEs. The fund's preliminary terms and conditions are detailed in Annex 2. Component 3: Project Management, Monitoring, and Evaluation (US$ 5 million). This component will consist of the activities of (i) project monitoring and project evaluation; (ii) fiduciary management, environmental and social safeguards compliance, and Paris alignment; (iii) technical engineering studies, social and environmental safeguards studies, and third-party technical audits civil works; (iv) expenses for day-to-day management and supervision of the project; (v) capacity building; (vi) services from a technical firm with expertise in engineering, contract management, site supervision, and road safety to augment PIU technical capabilities; and (vii) studies to inform activities that could be later supported during implementation and/or a subsequent phase of the Project. This component will also include civil works supervision. Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response Component (US$0): The Government of Tunisia may request to re-allocate project funds to this component to support response and reconstruction following a declared emergency. This component would allow the Government of Tunisia to request re-categorize and reallocate financing from other project components to partially cover emergency response and recovery costs. The component can also be used to channel additional funds, should they become available because of an emergency.
